dispute: Two parties agree on an animal's capacities, on the alternatives available, and on who decides, and still disagree about whether the animal's interests count.
source: Constructed by the model as a candidate counterexample to the option-distribution reading. Not drawn from a documented dispute. Offered, then found to reduce; recorded with the reduction rather than discarded.

sides.position: the animal's options enter the account

option_claims.note: options attributed to it are read from its behaviour under varied conditions

frame.boundary_criterion: capacity to have options at all

sides.position: the animal is part of the situation, not a party to it

option_claims.note: treated as a feature of the environment the decision is made about

cuts_required.cut: how borderline members of the admitted species are handled

residue_candidates.claim: the two sides hold different values about animals
residue_candidates.note: The dispute is over whether one party's optionality enters the tally. That is a boundary decision on the option distribution, not a difference in what either side values. Both sides weight admitted parties the same way.

residue_candidates.claim: the excluding side simply cares less
residue_candidates.note: The excluding side holds the animal fixed, so nothing about it enters as a variable to care about. The apparent difference in caring is downstream of the held_fixed assignment.
